deed: IsraAID — הארגון הישראלי שהגיע ראשון להאיטי אחרי רעידת האדמה
title: IsraAID in Haiti: Israeli volunteers treated earthquake casualties and stayed for years to rebuild

trailer.text: IsraAID is an Israeli non-governmental organization for emergency aid around the world, and its founders are Shachar Zahavi and Mully Dor.
On January 12, 2010, a 7.0 magnitude earthquake struck Haiti, a poor country in the Caribbean.
According to JTA, an IsraAID team made up entirely of volunteers arrived in Port-au-Prince with 15 doctors, nurses, paramedics and logistics personnel.
The team immediately began treating the wounded at the site where a collapsed hospital had stood.

According to a joint opinion piece by IsraAID CEO Yotam Polizer and Brian Siegal of AJC, IsraAID staff were in Haiti in 2010 and remained there for another eight years, and so the organization has a well-established network of connections there.

glance.label: How long they stayed
glance.value: According to a joint article by the CEO of IsraAID and a person from AJC, staff members of the organization remained in Haiti for another eight years after 2010.

paragraphs.text: On January 12, 2010, a 7.0 magnitude earthquake struck Haiti.
According to the Jewish Virtual Library website, more than a million Haitians were left without a roof over their heads.
According to Israel21c, 300,000 people were injured.
According to JTA, most of Port-au-Prince had no power.
Civilian aid workers also had difficulty getting into the country.
The airport could not take in more aid flights, because the planes already on the ground there did not have enough fuel to take off.

stations.title: Messages in the middle of the night

paragraphs.text: Shachar Zahavi then headed IsraAID, an organization that coordinates 17 Israeli and Jewish aid organizations.
The organization was founded in 2001 as a collaboration of Israeli organizations.
According to JTA, the coalition includes, among others, FIRST, the Jerusalem AIDS Project and Pirchey Refua.
According to JTA, in the middle of the night messages began arriving on Zahavi's phone. Everyone was asking what was being done about Haiti.
By morning, preparations were under way to send an Israeli relief team.
But the way was blocked.
According to the Jewish Journal, on Friday the team was still looking for a way into Haiti from the Dominican Republic.
Zahavi said the team was considering flying from there, or renting a bus or off-road vehicles and driving across the border.
According to the Jewish Journal, an American organization called Operation Blessing sent a container of medical and relief supplies from Miami for the team's use.
According to JTA, the group arrived in Port-au-Prince on Saturday: 15 doctors, nurses, paramedics and logistics personnel.
They immediately began treating the wounded at the site where a collapsed hospital had stood.
According to an opinion piece written in 2021 by IsraAID CEO Yotam Polizer and Brian Siegal of AJC, a team from the organization was in Haiti just two days after the 2010 disaster.
According to JTA, Alan Schneider of IsraAID said that on previous missions in Chad, Sri Lanka, Myanmar, Kenya and Georgia he had not seen destruction on such a scale.

According to a text message from a member of the IsraAID team quoted by JTA, a six-year-old girl was pulled from the rubble by locals nearly six days after the earthquake, was treated by the IsraAID/FIRST medical team and survived, and was about to be transferred for further treatment to the IDF field hospital.
According to the Jewish Journal, after treatment at the IsraAID clinic she was transferred to the IDF field hospital.

According to the Jewish Virtual Library website, on 17 February, about a month after the earthquake, therapists from ALYN Hospital arrived in Haiti with the IsraAID team, and a five-year-old girl whose leg had been amputated began to walk with the help of crutches.
Zahavi said that IsraAID teams always carry an Israeli flag and hang it wherever they work, and that they do not operate under the radar.
He said it is important to them to show that they come on behalf of the Israeli people.
Dani Biran of Israel's mission to the UN said he was sure it is good for Israel's image, but that this is not the only reason for the effort.
According to JTA, the IsraAID team was just one part of the broad Israeli and Jewish effort to help Haiti.
According to the Jewish Virtual Library website, a 220-person delegation took off on January 14 in two 747 jets leased from El Al.
According to the same website, the delegation landed in Port-au-Prince on January 15, 2010.
It set up its operation center in a soccer field near the airport.
According to JTA, the five Magen David Adom paramedics reached Port-au-Prince only on Monday, overland, after landing in the Dominican Republic.

stations.title: The hospital near the soccer stadium

paragraphs.text: According to JTA, the IDF set up a field hospital near a soccer stadium.
It was one of the only places in the city where advanced medical treatment could be received.
On Saturday, Israeli doctors at the hospital delivered a baby boy, and his mother said she would name him Israel.
According to the Jewish Virtual Library website, the delegation treated more than 1,110 patients, performed 319 successful surgeries and assisted in 16 births.
According to JTA, an IDF rescue team pulled a Haitian man alive from the rubble on January 17, 2010, after an eight-hour effort.
According to the Jewish Journal, an Israeli team helped rescue two female students buried under the ruins of a university in Port-au-Prince.
According to JTA, ZAKA workers pulled eight students alive from the ruins of a university building.
Mati Goldstein, head of the ZAKA delegation, described the situation as true madness and the number of bodies as beyond grasp.
According to Israel21c, IsraAID's policy is to stay on the ground after the emergency and set up rehabilitation programs for the community.
Zahavi said the organization is not a hit-and-run organization, but stays for the long term to help victims rebuild their lives.
According to the Jewish Virtual Library website, Tevel b'Tzedek provided post-trauma treatment in the refugee camps, under the auspices of IsraAID.

According to Wikipedia, in February 2010 IsraAID, together with other bodies such as Operation Blessing, opened a children's education center in the Pétion-Ville refugee camp, the largest in the Port-au-Prince area.
Zahavi said the organization ran a medical facility, an agriculture program, a youth empowerment center and a program against gender violence in Haiti.
According to Israel21c, of 1.5 million people displaced from their homes, about 85,000 were still living in temporary tent cities in 2015.
That year, IsraAID was the only Israeli non-governmental organization still operating in Haiti.
According to Israel21c, Zahavi said that most of the money for the programs comes from donations by Jewish federations in North America.
According to Israel21c, the programs are gradually being handed over to Haitian organizations.
Ben Katzir, an Israeli who speaks Haitian Creole, arrived in Haiti in 2010 and stayed there for several years.
According to Israel21c, an IsraAID team had already been in Haiti for more than six years when Hurricane Matthew struck it in 2016.

According to Israel21c, Mickey Noam-Alon of IsraAID reported that IsraAID and its local partner Prodev were the first to provide food and water to hundreds of children and their families in Cite Soleil after the hurricane.
According to Israel21c, Israel does not have a resident embassy in Haiti.
According to IsraAID's CEO, thanks to its long years in Haiti the organization has a well-established network of connections there.
According to the Jerusalem Post, in 2021 IsraAID sent an emergency team to Haiti after an earthquake that claimed more than 1,200 lives.
The CEO, Yotam Polizer, said that Haiti is one of the most disaster-vulnerable places in the world.
According to Polizer and Brian Siegal, in IsraAID's approach psychological first aid is as essential as food, water and shelter.

claims.text: IsraAID היא ארגון לא ממשלתי ישראלי הפועל לסיוע בחירום ברחבי העולם.
claims.quote: IsraAID (The Israel Forum for International Humanitarian Aid) is an Israel-based, non-governmental organization (NGO) that responds to emergencies all over the world with targeted humanitarian help.

claims.text: לפי ויקיפדיה, IsraAID נוסדה על ידי שחר זהבי ומולי דור.
claims.quote: IsraAID was founded by Shachar Zahavi and Mully Dor.

claims.text: ב-12 בינואר 2010 פגעה בהאיטי, המדינה ענייה בים הקריבי, רעידת אדמה בעוצמה של 7.0.
claims.quote: On January 12, 2010, a 7.0 magnitude earthquake struck the impoverished nation of Haiti in the Caribbean.

claims.text: לפי JTA, קבוצה של 15 רופאים, אחיות, פראמדיקים ואנשי לוגיסטיקה הגיעה ביום שבת לפורט-או-פרנס והחלה מיד לטפל בפצועים באתר בית חולים שקרס.
claims.quote: Consisting of doctors, nurses, paramedics and logistics experts, the 15-person group arrived Saturday in Port-au-Prince and immediately set to work treating wounded Haitians at the site of a collapsed hospital near the city center.

claims.text: לפי JTA, צוות IsraAid הורכב כולו ממתנדבים והיה רק חלק מהמאמץ הישראלי והיהודי הרחב לסייע להאיטי.
claims.quote: The IsraAid team, comprised fully of volunteers, was just one component of the broad Israeli and Jewish effort to help Haiti.

claims.text: לפי מנכ"ל IsraAID, צוות הארגון נשאר בהאיטי עוד שמונה שנים אחרי 2010, ולכן יש רשת קשרים מבוססת.
claims.quote: Because IsraAID staff were on hand in 2010 and remained in Haiti for another eight years, there is a network of well-established connections in place

claims.text: לפי ג'רוזלם פוסט, IsraAID נוסדה ב-2001 כשיתוף פעולה של ארגונים ישראליים והפכה לארגון הסיוע החירומי הגדול בישראל.

claims.quote: the tens of strong aftershocks that came in its wake, led to the death of an estimated 320,000 and left more than a million Haitians homeless.

claims.text: לפי ישראל21c, לפחות 230,000 האיטים מתו בעקבות רעידת האדמה של 2010 ו-300,000 נפצעו.
claims.quote: At least 230,000 Haitians died as a result of the 2010 earthquake, and 300,000 people were injured.

claims.text: לפי ישראל21c, צוות IsraAID היה בהאיטי יותר משש שנים כשפגע הוריקן מתיו ב-2016, והגיע מיד אחרי הרעידה.
claims.quote: A crew from the nonprofit organization IsraAID has been in Haiti for more than six years, having arrived just after the January 2010 earthquake to help in rescue and recovery operations.

claims.text: לפי ישראל21c, IsraAID ושותפה המקומי Prodev סיפקו ראשונים מזון ומים בסיטה סולייל בעקבות ההוריקן ב-2016.
claims.quote: IsraAID and local partner Prodev were the first to provide food and water for hundreds of children and their families at Cite Soleil

claims.text: לפי ישראל21c, לישראל אין שגרירות תושבת בהאיטי.
claims.quote: Israel does not have a resident embassy in Haiti.

claims.text: לפי ג'רוזלם פוסט, ב-2021 שלחה IsraAID צוות חירום להאיטי אחרי רעידת אדמה שגבתה מעל 1,200 חיים.
claims.quote: The Israeli NGO IsraAID has sent assistance to Haiti after a catastrophic earthquake claimed the lives of over 1,200 people, the organization said on Sunday.

claims.text: מנכ"ל IsraAID יותם פוליזר אמר שהאיטי היא אחד המקומות הפגיעים ביותר לאסונות בעולם.
claims.quote: Haiti is one of the most disaster-vulnerable places in the world and communities across the country have been through so much in recent years

claims.text: לפי פוליזר ובריאן סיגל, בגישת IsraAID עזרה ראשונה נפשית חיונית כמו מזון, מים ומחסה.
claims.quote: Providing psychological first aid is as essential as food, water and shelter.

claims.text: לפי אלן שניידר, חבר במשלחת, IsraAID הייתה הצוות הראשון בשטח בעת רעידת האדמה של 2010.
claims.quote: IsraAID had sent assistance to Haiti during its 2010 earthquake disaster and was the first team on the ground, according to Alan Schneider, a member of that mission.

claims.text: לפי JTA, צה"ל היה הצוות הישראלי הגדול הראשון שהגיע להאיטי.
claims.quote: The Israel Defense Forces was the first major Israeli team to arrive.

claims.text: לפי אתר הספרייה היהודית הווירטואלית, המשלחת הישראלית כללה 236 חברים, מהם 218 חיילים וקצינים ו-18 אזרחים.
claims.quote: The delegation's 236 members, including 218 IDF soldiers and officers and 18 civilians, returned to Ben-Gurion International Airport in Tel Aviv the following day.

claims.text: לפי ישראל21c, תוך 24 שעות מהרעידה שלח משרד החוץ הישראלי צוות של 220 איש.
claims.quote: Within 24 hours of the severe earthquake that rocked Haiti on January 12, 2010, Israel’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs sent a 220-person team of rescuers, disaster-management experts and medical personnel.

claims.text: לפי ה-Jewish Journal, צה"ל הודיע ביום שלישי שבית החולים השדה וצוות החילוץ יישארו בהאיטי לפחות עוד חודש.
claims.quote: the IDF announced Tuesday that the Israeli field hospital and rescue crew will remain in Haiti for at least another month.

claims.text: לפי אתר הספרייה היהודית הווירטואלית, צוות הרפואה והחילוץ של צה"ל סיים את פעילותו ב-27 בינואר 2010.
claims.quote: The IDF medical and rescue team concluded its operations on January 27, 2010.
